add.title: The size of the stylesheet is not the cause of the slow lab; the CSS work of the primitive layer is
add.measured: 42% to 71% of the main thread time of a page
add.summary: Chrome parses the 475 KB sheet in 5 to 13 ms and a sheet of double size changes nothing; with an empty sheet the main thread work of one page goes down by 42% to 71% in the production form. Three checkers do not agree on the cost of rules that match no element (0 to about 40% of the style time).
add.confidence: high for the direction, low for the exact share: the load average was 12 to 850
evidence: perf/README.md, sections 'The answer in short' and 'The size of the file'

add.title: Live preview frames are about 94% of the wait of the lab gallery
add.measured: 9 to 19 s against about 1 s in development
add.summary: The gallery is 10 to 16 full apps in one page: 4,895 requests in development. With the frame documents blocked, the gallery is usable after about 1 s in development and 0.5 s in the production form. The real app is one document, so it does not have this cost.
add.confidence: high: two lanes and a checker measured it

add.title: The hover glider of a nav makes one key press recalculate the whole list
add.measured: 1,245 of 1,734 elements for one arrow key; 87 with the bar glider only
add.summary: The two hover rules of navGlider have `.nav:not(:has(...)) > &`, so the nav is the anchor of a `:has()` that is not in the subject, and with the rule shape of PERF-04 Chrome invalidates its subtree at each change inside it. Arrow key: 96 ms to the next frame as built, 48 ms with the bar glider only. A rewrite of the two rules with the `:has()` in the subject gives 71 elements in the largest recalculation with four gliders, and equal pictures.
add.confidence: high for the counts (the same in each run); the times are ratios from a busy machine
evidence: record/counts.mjs with record/rotate.sh -> record/results/R-large-g-hover-bar.log, R-large-g-nohover.log, R-large-fixhover.log, R-large-fix2.log

add.title: Ten recipe class names make a `:has()` rule shape that lets each `:has()` anchor invalidate its whole subtree
add.measured: 1,245 against 180 recalculated elements for one arrow key
add.summary: A compound with `:has()`, then a combinator, then `*` (also inside `:is()` or `:not()`) puts 'the whole subtree' into the one invalidation set that Chrome keeps for `:has()` outside the subject. The lab sheet has 23 such rules and the sheet of apps/web has 8, from `ui-disabled-within`, `ui-field-disabled`, `ui-choice-on`, and `ui-choice-disabled` with `**:`, `*:`, `group-.../name:`, and `not-...:`. The removal of the 10 class names is a test: it changes disabled and checked choice controls. Nobody tested a rewrite.
add.confidence: high for the effect; the mechanism inside Chrome is read from the trace and from experiments
evidence: record/patch.py, change 'norules' -> record/results/A-large-1x.log, rows norules and norules-rm3

add.title: Three recipe class names make a sibling rule shape: each element that is added or removed recalculates the subtree of its parent
add.measured: 2,481 of 2,589 elements for one arrow key; 127 without the 3 rules
add.summary: `not-peer-ui-focus-visible:outline-none`, `not-ui-sibling-selected:hidden`, and `not-peer-ui-focus-visible:invisible` compile to `X ~ *` where an alternative of X is only a pseudo-class (`:focus-visible`, `:checked`). Chrome then invalidates the subtree of the parent at each insertion or removal of an element. A tooltip of Ariakit adds a portal node to the body, so the whole document is recalculated. Each of the 3 rules alone keeps the cost. A rewrite of the two custom variants (`ui-focus-visible` as a selector list, `:checked:where(.control)` in `ui-sibling-selected`) gives 129 elements and equal pictures; the sheet grows by 6,646 bytes. apps/web has the same 3 class names.
add.confidence: high for the lab; counted from code and not measured for apps/web
evidence: record/sheet-variants.mjs with spec-B2.json, spec-B3.json, spec-B4.json -> record/results/B2-synthetic.log, B3-synthetic.log, B4-synthetic.log

add.title: The variant control of the settled design mounts new tooltips for each screenshot
add.measured: 3 portal nodes removed and 3 added for one arrow key
add.summary: `VariantPager` gives each mark the key of its variant, so a new screenshot removes each `Hint` and adds a new one, and each tooltip has a portal node in the body. With PERF-05 this is one recalculation of the document for each key. With the key of the place, one arrow key recalculates 45 elements and needs 108 ms in place of 341 ms at 585 rows; a screenshot with another number of variants still pays.

add.title: The typed registered properties of @ariakit/tailwind are not the style cost: they limit the cost of the layer formulas
add.measured: 57 µs for each element of a full recalculation; 18 µs without the 51 typed rules
add.summary: Without the 51 typed `@property` rules a full recalculation is 69% faster, but the page is broken (83% of the pixels differ). The same rules with `syntax: "*"` are slower: 14 times for the 14 colors and 6.7 times for the 11 lengths, and no change for the 26 numbers (equal picture, 8% to 11% more time). `inherits: true` on the 32 rules that have `false`: 7% more time. Without the class `ak-layer` on the 304 transparent layers that change nothing: 10% less time, and 3% to 5% of the pixels differ. The time goes away only where a removal breaks the formulas that `ak-layer` writes. No faster form with an equal picture was found.
add.confidence: high for the ranking; one page, one browser, a full recalculation after a theme switch and not a page load
evidence: record/properties.mjs (pictures of a page load) with record/diff-pictures.mjs -> record/results/C-pictures-load.log

add.title: Rows rendered in parts do not help at 41 rows and halve the arrow key at 585 rows
add.measured: 133 ms against 55 ms at 585 rows, after the rewrite of PERF-05
add.summary: `content-visibility: auto` with `contain-intrinsic-block-size` on each row keeps keyboard navigation, focus, and the glider anchor. The picture is not equal: the content of a row moves by a part of a pixel (3,126 of 172,640 pixels of the list at 41 rows). At 41 rows only 13 rows skip their content and a scroll has 2 to 4 times more layouts with a glider. At 585 rows it does not remove the recalculation of PERF-05 (1,958 of 2,590 elements), and after that fix it cuts the arrow key from 133 ms to 55 ms. A window of visible rows was not built.
add.confidence: medium: CSS added in the browser, not a change of the source

add.title: With the CPU slowed 4 times, the arrow key and Approve of the settled review page are far above 200 ms as built, and at the line with the bar glider only
add.measured: 438 to 515 ms as built, 188 to 276 ms with the bar glider only
add.summary: 41 rows, production form, three sessions at a load average of 50 to 78, 41 to 61, and 22 to 43. Arrow key: 515, 438, and 457 ms as built; 276, 188, and 198 ms with the bar glider only. Approve: 555, 497, and 480 ms as built; 305, 225, and 230 ms with the bar glider only. With the bar glider only, style and layout are 88 ms of the 276 ms, so the rest is script. With no throttle the two forms need 96 and 48 ms. A quiet machine was not available, so the 200 ms line is not settled for the forms near it.
add.confidence: medium: the ratios are stable, the absolute times are from a busy machine
evidence: record/options.mjs -> record/results/A-large-4x.log, A2-large-g-nohover-4x.log, A2-large-fix2-4x.log, and results/SUMMARY.txt

add.title: The development server multiplies the script time of an interaction by 3.8 to 5.7
add.summary: React development mode with StrictMode, and unbundled modules: one preview is 363 requests and about 20 MB in development against 104 requests in the production form. Style and layout are equal in both forms. Judge the speed of a design in the production form: `vite build`, then `vite preview`.
